newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit overshoots 96 goal in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit overshoots 96 goal in Sept.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose to 81.9 billion levs at the end of September, overshooting the 1996 deficit target by 1.5 percent, local media said, quoting finance ministry officials.
The deficit rose by 10.1 billion levs from 71.8 billion levs in mid-September, figures showed.
Finance ministry officials were not available for comment.

Expenditure rose by 27.6 billion levs to 282.6 billion levs in the second half of September, which is 64.4 percent of the 1996 target. Revenue grew by 17.5 billion levs to 200.7 billion levs, or 56 percent of the target.
"The large rise in the deficit was due to large domestic debt payments and low tax revenue," Standart daily quoted finance ministry officials as saying.
The deficit also rose sharply because part of tax revenues were blocked in banks put under special supervision by the central bank two weeks ago due to a danger of insolvency, 24 Chasa daily said.
A record high central interest rate (CIR), in effect for two weeks now, was expected to exert a drastic strain on domestic debt servicing, experts said.
The central bank hiked the CIR to 25 percent monthly, or 300 percent annually from 108 percent, to try to restore confidence in the fragile lev currency and crumbling local banks.
Cumulative annual yield of government securities with maturity of up to one year now ranges between 602 and 2407 percent, central bank data showed.
If the central rate is not cut soon or if tax collection does not improve, a second budget revision will become necessary before year-end, Standart said.
Bulgaria's parliament on July 30 revised the annual budget to meet higher foreign and domestic debt payments and keep the structural reform on track.

Revenue was set at 358.2 billion levs and spending at 438.9 billion levs. The deficit was assumed at 4.9 percent of gross domestic product or 80.7 billion levs, up from the original 58.3 billion levs.
Under the revised 1996 budget, Bulgaria will allocate 52.6 percent, or 231 billion levs, of expenditure planned for the year to cover interest payments on foreign and domestic debt.

The government's domestic debt rose to some 600 billion levs at the end of August from 345 billion levs at the beginning of the year. The Finance Ministry has recently started to cover maturity payments on treasury paper with fresh issues of government securities. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 84561
